To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the 5-nitrotizazole derivatives were found to be active against both log phase and non-replicating MTB.
the 5-nitrofuran-2-carboamide derivatives are active against both replicative (MIC 5.48 µM) and non-replicating (MIC 2.74 µM) M. tuberculosis.
5-nitromethylthiazole derivatives have been synthesized and evaluated for their antitubercular activities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel 5-nitrotiazole derivatives as potential leads against both replicating and non-replicating forms of MTB.
the development of new 5-nitrotiazole derivatives as antituberculosis agents.
the development of new nitrothiazole-based compounds with potential antitubercular activity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

5-nitrosalicylic acid and 5-nitrofurfural are two key moieties in the development of 5-nitrated thiazoles against M. tuberculosis, especially for the compounds that target both replicative and non-replicative MTB.

the compounds 20, 21, 22, and 23 are promising candidates for the treatment of TB and further studies are needed to determine whether these compounds can effectively kill intracellular bacteria in macrophage cells.
the 5-nitromethylfuran-2-carbonyl moiety is a promising pharmacophore for anti-tubercular drug discovery.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
5-nitromethylthiazole-2-carboxamides and 5-nitrofuran-2-carboamides were identified as novel lead compounds for MTB.
5-nitrofuran-2-carbaldehyde (5) is a good starting point to synthesize 5-nitrotizol-2-amine derivatives with potential for further optimization.
the 5-nitrotiazole derivatives are potential lead compounds for the development of new antituberculosis drugs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
5-nitrosulfonyl thiazole derivatives can be considered as a new class of antitubercular agents with activity against drug-sensitive and multidrug resistant (MDR) strains of M. tuberculosis.
the 5-nitrofuran moiety is a good substituent on the 5-nitorthiazole core for the development of novel antitubercular agents.
the compounds with a 5-nitrofuran ring attached at the 2-position of thiazole ring are more potent and less cytotoxic than the ones having a 5-nitrouracil ring attached at the same position.
